doc.title: Sheila Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Middleburgh, New York, May 11, 2002

title: First bass-and-voice performances: Mingus, Steve Swallow, Cameron Brown
summary: She explains why she loved the bass, the Blue Note trio with Barry Galbraith, her first duo with Mingus on Yesterdays, and later work with Swallow, Cameron Brown and Harvey Schwartz.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Was it a conscious thing at that time? I mean sometimes those things — I’ve heard stories about well this saxophone, this bass thing happened simply because the other people didn’t show up.

Oh no mine was like, mine was I loved the bass. And I remember thinking — actually my Blue Note album, I wanted it to be bass and voice but it was a little bit — nobody wanted to take that chance yet. But thanks to George Russell, who got me the Blue Note date, had made it a trio with guitar, Barry Galbraith, the wonderful Barry Galbraith, and so it was pretty similar but not quite. And there were a couple of things I did with bass and Denzil Best on drums. But originally I wanted that to be a bass and voice. But I had been into the bass and voice and practicing it and doing it, because I loved the sound of the bass, and then Peggy Lee came out with that “Fever.” And the same thing happened with a string quartet I wanted to do years ago. And Stan Getz came out with “Focus.” So I said you know, then I’m not so crazy. And well Peggy Lee only did one tune, and I think she had drums too on “Fever,” but I really had been doing it just with the bass. Actually my first bass partner, the first time I ever performed it was with Charles Mingus in Toledo. And he said, “Well why don’t you come up and sing with us.” And I’d been sort of doing it a lot, but Lennie Tristano is one I was studying with, Lennie, and different sessions, but never out anywhere. And I said, “Well there’s no piano.” And he said, “Well that shouldn’t bother you.” And I said, “Oh well that’s true.” And so I did a duo with Charles Mingus. And I’ll never forget it. It was “Yesterdays.” It was “Yesterdays” in G minor. And now I do “Yesterdays” in F minor, so my voice hasn’t changed that much.

Yeah, exactly one step, right. But I remember that. And then I grabbed Steve Swallow, because he used to work at this club in the Village where I worked a couple of nights a week and on Monday nights he’d come in and play, and I started doing the things with him and then every once in a while we’d do a little date together. There was a club in the Village that did a lot of sort of avante garde type music called the Take Three, and it was upstairs. And we would go up there, carry the bass up there and do this concert. wonderful. Yeah. And I’ve been doing it ever since. It’s just that now I’ve gotten back together with Cameron Brown. Because originally he had rehearsed bass and voice with me but then he got very busy with some of the other musicians you know. And he couldn’t rehearse as much. And then Harvey of course came in to the picture from the Steve Kuhn Quartet.
